O.outcome_detail: mandatory OSCE assessing history-taking, physical examination and diagnosis of actor-patients

cells.quote: The results of the OSCE revealed no differences between the groups.
cells.note: Equivalence was not tested, so the non-significant result is inconclusive rather than evidence of equivalence.

D.treatment: voluntary basic skills-lab sessions relevant to the OSCE
D.comparison: voluntary advanced skills-lab sessions without reference to the OSCE

O.outcome_detail: mean number of voluntary skills-lab attendances per student

cells.quote: The mean number of attendances per student at voluntary skills-lab training showed a significantly higher average value for voluntary basic skills-lab training sessions (1.84±1.91 participations) than for voluntary advanced skills-lab training sessions (0.92±1.17 participations; p<0.001).
cells.note: Retrospective descriptive analysis of attendance records for 340 third-year medical students across two terms; attendance session type was not experimentally assigned.

D.treatment: procedural-skills OSCE with direct observation and examiner feedback
D.comparison: procedure logs as the current assessment method

O.outcome_detail: perceived usefulness of the assessment as a formative learning opportunity

cells.quote: The participants found their participation in the procedural skills OSCE particularly rewarding since “[it] is the only evaluation system we have thus far. I mean I would like to see a more complex evaluation system, a little bit more realistic. But for now, I think examining assigned procedural skills [via the OSCE] is a good idea” (Resident 3.3).
cells.note: Residents viewed the OSCE more positively than procedure logs, but this was a qualitative perception rather than a quantitative comparison.

D.treatment: OSCE-based direct observation with immediate expert feedback
D.comparison: clinical procedural practice with sporadic or absent expert feedback

O.outcome_detail: perceived benefit of supervision and feedback for learning procedural skills

cells.quote: Participants explained that the most important aspect of the OSCE station was the opportunity to learn with experts (staff physicians) who were not only supervising them but also giving them immediate feedback. As one participant explained: “the main benefit of the exam was getting the supervision…as artificial as the feedback was in the exam setting; it is hugely beneficial in terms of what my lack of knowledge is” (Resident 2.1).
cells.note: The study reports residents' perceptions of the value of expert observation and feedback, not an objective learning effect.

O.outcome_detail: science learning outcomes and academic gains

cells.quote: Experiences in informal settings can significantly improve science learning outcomes for individuals from groups which are historically underrepresented in science, such as women and minorities. Evaluations of museum -based and after-school programs suggest that these programs may also support academic gains for children and youth in these groups.
cells.note: The study reports a research-based synthesis citing Bell et al. (2009), but does not specify the comparison condition, included-study designs, participant expertise, or outcome timing. The text names children and youth and also refers more broadly to individuals, so age is coded mixed.
